drivingQuestion: Is damage driven by the animal's inclination but without intent to harm treated like Goring?

segments.he: בָּעֵי רַב עֵינָא: כִּשְׁכְּשָׁה בְּאַמָּתָהּ מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַקֶּרֶן – קֶרֶן לָאו יִצְרָא קָתָקֵיף לֵיהּ? הָכָא נָמֵי לָא שְׁנָא; אוֹ דִלְמָא, קֶרֶן כַּוּוֹנָתוֹ לְהַזִּיק, הָא אֵין כַּוּוֹנָתָהּ לְהַזִּיק? תֵּיקוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Eina raises a dilemma:» If an animal «swung its penis» and caused damage, «what is» the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: «Do we say just as it is with regard to Goring: Is it not» so in a case of «Goring» that the animal’s «inclination overcame it» and caused it to gore? «Here too, it is no different:» The animal’s inclination overcame it and that is why it caused damage. «Or perhaps» the cases are different, as in the case of damage in the category of «Goring» the «objective» of «its» action «is to cause damage,» whereas in «this» case the «objective» of «its» action «is not to cause damage.» The Gemara concludes: This dilemma «shall stand» unresolved.
